name: Stork
overview: The stork is presented in Scripture both as a physical bird and as a figurative symbol. It is identified as one of the birds forbidden for consumption, emphasizing God's holiness in dietary laws (Leviticus 11:19). The stork's natural behavior is highlighted in its nesting habits in fir trees (Psalms 104:17) and its migratory patterns, which demonstrate an instinctive knowledge of appointed times, contrasting with Israel's failure to recognize God's judgment (Jeremiah 8:7). Additionally, the stork's wings serve as a vivid image in prophetic vision, symbolizing swift movement and divine activity (Zechariah 5:9).
